newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate up on month-end liquidity lack.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate up on month-end liquidity lack.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates were 70 basis points higher at 18.00 percent due to month-end demand for liquidity and a soft peso, traders said.
"We were expecting secondary rates to hold steady at the open, but they increased on lack of liquidity and a slide in the peso," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso was 1.15 centavos weaker at 7.9135/7.9165 per dollar in early dealing.
Dealers said liquidity shortages took them by surprise, and prevented secondary rates declining in line with early decreases in yields on the U.S. long bond.

"The end of the month is lending itself to a little speculation, furthermore next week sees the central bank cut off date, which is also putting pressure on liquidity. The long bond isn't helping much," another trader said.
Banks have until next Wednesday to settle balances outstanding on checking accounts they hold with the central bank.
Fixed-income analysts said much market liquidity had been drained in recent weeks by central bank participation composed of direct Cetes sales assigned at maturities of up to one year.
U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds were meanwhile up 18/32 to yield 6.93 percent.
Overnight rates on bank paper were up 20 basis points at 19.00 percent.

Liquidity of 2.773 billion pesos was due to return to the system from prior central bank participation. Nonetheless, dealers expected liquidity of 1.5 billion to flow out of the system to fund a tax bill for state oil corporation Petroleos Mexicanos.
In addition, traders forecast a drain of one billion pesos in bank bills for weekend consumer spending and month-end payrolls.
